name: Somatropin
route_note: subcutaneous injection, usually daily in the evening by pen; weekly long-acting analogues are separate INNs
owner: Novo Nordisk, Pfizer, Merck KGaA, Eli Lilly, Sandoz, Ferring and others

discovery.by: Choh Hao Li and Harold Papkoff (isolation of human GH); Genentech (recombinant, 1979)
discovery.note: Human growth hormone was first purified from cadaver pituitaries; recombinant production in E. coli followed in 1979.

rx_status: prescription (US distribution restricted by law to approved indications)
tagline: Recombinant growth hormone, which replaced cadaver GH after prion disease cases
summary: Somatropin is recombinant human growth hormone with the natural 191-amino-acid sequence. It treats growth failure in children with GH deficiency and several genetic and other conditions, and adult GH deficiency; it replaced pituitary-extracted GH after cases of Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease in 1985. Omnitrope was the first biosimilar approved in Europe.
mechanism: Somatropin binds the growth hormone receptor, causing receptor dimerisation and activation of JAK2–STAT5 signalling. In the liver and other tissues this induces insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1), which mediates much of the growth-promoting effect at the epiphyseal growth plates.
GH also has direct metabolic effects: it increases lipolysis and protein synthesis, decreases fat mass and antagonises insulin action on glucose uptake.
uses: Growth hormone deficiency in children and adults
Small for gestational age without catch-up growth

history.title: Pituitary GH therapy
history.detail: Maurice Raben first treats a GH-deficient child with human pituitary growth hormone.

history.title: Recombinant GH
history.detail: Genentech produces human growth hormone in E. coli.

history.title: CJD and recombinant approval
history.detail: Pituitary-derived GH is withdrawn after Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease cases; FDA approves recombinant Protropin.

history.title: Natural-sequence somatropin
history.detail: Eli Lilly's Humatrope, identical to native GH, is approved in the US.

history.title: First EU biosimilar
history.detail: Sandoz's Omnitrope becomes the first biosimilar approved in the European Union.

history.title: Weekly analogues arrive
history.detail: Long-acting GH analogues begin to be approved, starting with somapacitan (Sogroya) in adults.

pk.half_life: about 2–3 h after SC injection (about 20 min IV)

serious: respiratory death in severely obese Prader–Willi patients

facts: Omnitrope (2006) was the first biosimilar of any kind approved in the European Union.
Over 200 cases of Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease worldwide have been linked to cadaveric pituitary growth hormone.
